key_insight: A multi-fidelity transfer-learning pipeline using a convolutional autoencoder can learn guided-wave damage patterns from large simulated data and adapt effectively to scarce experimental measurements.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical, low-cost structural health monitoring for plate-like structures with piezoelectric transducers when labeled experimental damage data are limited.
method: Generate a large synthetic pretraining set with a lightweight 1D time-domain spectral element model.
Train a convolutional autoencoder to learn compact guided-wave features, then transfer them to a feed-forward damage predictor.
Fine-tune the model on a small labeled experimental dataset to localize and size damage.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong generalization, with R² above 0.93 for damage localization and above 0.99 for damage sizing on unseen damage cases.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the simulated wave physics match the experimental domain, so domain shift and sensor/actuator placement must be carefully managed.
paper_title: A Multi-Fidelity Convolutional Autoencoder-Transfer Learning Framework for Guided-Wave-Based Damage Diagnosis Using Large Simulated and Limited Experimental Datasets
